summary: Verified by direct HTTP checks on 2026-09-16 (no browser execution tests). Pyodide 314.0.7 is the latest release and loads from jsdelivr with open CORS; first load is about 13.5 MB of assets, cached afterwards. Monaco 0.56.0 is on cdnjs and npm, but its CDN build now uses hashed chunk filenames and a worker that is cross-origin when loaded from a CDN, which makes a no-build Monaco setup brittle. CodeMirror 6 is ESM-only with no official UMD build. A Vite build (Vite 8.3, npm monaco-editor or CodeMirror 6, Pyodide in a module Web Worker) avoids those problems. Pages opened via file:// break Web Workers, ES modules and fetch of local JSON, so the app should be served over http (GitHub Pages, Netlify, vite preview, or python3 -m http.server).

findings.detail: npm dist-tags: latest 314.0.7, stable-0.29 0.29.5, next 315.0.0-alpha.2. https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v314.0.7/full/pyodide.js and pyodide.mjs return HTTP 200 with access-control-allow-origin *. Also installable as npm package pyodide@314.0.7.

pyodide.asm.wasm 9,598,218 bytes; python_stdlib.zip 2,545,637; pyodide.asm.mjs 1,250,344; pyodide-lock.json 119,077; pyodide.js 18,912. Roughly 13.5 MB uncompressed first load; browser HTTP cache makes later loads fast. The old path pyodide.asm.js is 404 in 314.x (now .mjs).

cdnjs and npm latest is 0.56.0. min/vs/loader.js (AMD) and min/vs/editor/editor.main.js still exist and use define(), but the build is now Vite-produced hashed chunks: min/vs/editor-KLE6jdfb.js, min/vs/python-CqWUUgfu.js (Python tokenizer included), min/vs/assets/editor.worker-lj3bdIIn.js. Old paths min/vs/base/worker/workerMain.js and min/vs/basic-languages/python/python.js return 404. editor.main.js computes the worker URL with require.toUrl relative to the CDN, so the worker is cross-origin and needs a MonacoEnvironment.getWorkerUrl blob or data-URL proxy; hashed names make that proxy version-specific. Python has no language-service worker, so only the base editor worker matters.

codemirror 6.0.2, @codemirror/lang-python 6.2.1, @codemirror/view 6.43.12. ESM-only packages with no official UMD bundle on cdnjs, so it needs a bundler. Much smaller than Monaco (a few hundred KB), better on touch devices, themeable, but less VS Code-like out of the box (no minimap, simpler command palette).

npm latest: vite 8.3.0, react 19.3.0, typescript 7.0.2 (native compiler), vitest 5.0.1, @monaco-editor/react 4.7.0. Dev machine has Node 26.0.0, npm 11.12.1, Python 3.12.13, no pnpm or bun. With Vite, monaco-editor ESM plus ?worker imports is the documented integration and bundles the worker same-origin.
Chart.js 4.5.1 available on cdnjs as UMD and on npm. Google Fonts css2 endpoint returns 200.

findings.topic: file:// limitations (known platform behaviour, not browser-tested this session)
findings.detail: From a file:// page: ES module scripts with src fail on CORS, fetch() of local JSON fails, and new Worker('./worker.js') fails in Chrome. Blob-URL workers generally work. Cross-origin CDN fetches with ACAO * work. Therefore serving over http is strongly preferred.

Load Pyodide inside a dedicated Web Worker so the UI never freezes. Capture output with pyodide.setStdout({batched}) and setStderr. input() uses pyodide.setStdin({stdin}), which is synchronous: simplest is a pre-supplied stdin queue per run (question test cases provide stdin lines); interactive input needs SharedArrayBuffer + Atomics.wait, which requires cross-origin isolation (COOP/COEP headers; GitHub Pages cannot set headers, a coi-serviceworker shim exists).

Option 1: main thread sets a timer and calls worker.terminate(), then respawns the worker (Pyodide reload from HTTP cache takes roughly 1-3 s). Works with no special headers. Option 2: pyodide.setInterruptBuffer with a SharedArrayBuffer to raise KeyboardInterrupt, needs COOP/COEP. Option 3: a sys.settrace line-count or time budget installed inside Python that raises a friendly TimeoutError without killing the worker; slows execution but acceptable for beginner-sized programs.

Compile student code with compile(src, '<student>', 'exec') and exec into a fresh namespace dict; read traceback frames whose filename is '<student>' to get the editor line number without wrapper offsets. Hidden tests run as a Python harness that calls the student function per test case, compares with expected (math.isclose for floats, normalised whitespace for printed output), captures exception type/message per test, and returns a JSON string to JS.

localStorage: about 5 MB per origin, synchronous, strings only; fine for settings and progress summaries. IndexedDB: async, far larger quota, good for an append-only event log and code snapshots (thousands of records). Small wrappers: idb-keyval or Dexie. Provide JSON export/import for backup and moving between machines. Data stays on the student's device.
Pyodide supports current Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Safari 16.4+. Each Pyodide instance uses roughly 50-100 MB of memory, so keep one shared worker instance rather than one per question.

recommendations: Serve over http, never rely on file://. GitHub Pages or Netlify for sharing; npm run dev or python3 -m http.server locally.

If staying no-build, Monaco from cdnjs needs a version-pinned worker proxy and is brittle with 0.56 hashed chunks; if using Vite, install monaco-editor or CodeMirror 6 from npm and bundle workers same-origin.
Run Pyodide in one long-lived Web Worker, start loading it as soon as the landing page opens, and show a status indicator (loading / ready / running).
Default timeout: sys.settrace budget for a friendly 'possible infinite loop' message, with worker.terminate() plus respawn as a hard backstop after about 5 s.
Model input() with a stdin panel whose lines are queued before Run; questions that need input supply their own stdin.
Store an append-only event log and code snapshots in IndexedDB, progress and settings in localStorage, with JSON export/import.
openQuestions: Not browser-tested this session: the Monaco 0.56 CDN worker proxy with hashed names, a Pyodide worker started from file://, and sys.settrace overhead on loop-heavy code.
Whether the student will use the app offline; if so, a service worker to cache Pyodide assets is worth adding.
